title: Circular dependencies
context: How does Spring handle circular dependencies?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A circular dependency means bean A needs B and B needs A. With constructor injection Spring cannot create either first, so it fails at startup with BeanCurrentlyInCreationException. With setter or field injection, Spring used three-level caches to expose a half-built bean early and break the cycle. Spring Boot 2.6 and later disallow circular references by default. The right fix is to break the cycle: move the shared logic into a third bean, or use events, rather than re-enabling the setting.

points.title: Constructor cycles fail
points.why: A constructor needs the other bean already built, so the cycle can't start.

points.title: Break the cycle
points.why: Extract the shared logic into a third bean, or publish an event, instead of allowing cycles.
